latencyStats.description: Latency distribution for one measurement series, in milliseconds. Percentiles are null when count is too small to compute them honestly.

jitterAvg.description: Mean absolute difference between consecutive samples, in milliseconds.

description: One structured result from a single diagnostic check. Every platform implementation produces results in this shape so that reports, history, and troubleshooting rules stay comparable across platforms.

check.description: The diagnostic check that produced this result.

confidence.description: How strongly the evidence supports the explanation. Filtering verdicts require corroborating evidence and must not be reported as high confidence from a single signal.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock duration of the check itself, in milliseconds.

code.description: Platform error code in text form (for example an errno or WinSock value), when available.

explanation.description: Plain-language statement of what was measured and what it means. Facts only; hypotheses belong to the troubleshooting layer, not to a raw result.

measurement.description: Measured values, present when the check produced any. Null when the check failed before measuring.

resolver.description: Resolver that produced the answer, when known (DNS checks).

protocol.description: Protocol the measurement was taken at. Latency figures from different protocols are not interchangeable and must stay labelled.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this schema the result was written against.

status.description: Outcome of the check. 'blocked' is reserved for evidence of an intermediary preventing the connection (for example a reset during the TLS handshake); it must not be used for ordinary failures.

timestamp.description: When the check started, RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 with timezone.

verdict.description: Optional classification when this single result is conclusive on its own. Session-level verdicts live in the report summary.

title: NetScope Diagnostic Result
